title: Remove resume kernel parameters when removing hibernation
head: e870b4b31a25
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Upgrade-preserved resume parameters remain in /etc/default/limine after deleting resume.conf
leads.consequence: When the Quattro upgrade needs to recover a missing root=, it copies resume= and resume_offset= from the running /proc/cmdline into /etc/default/limine. That file loads after /etc/limine-entry-tool.d and its += value remains when resume.conf is removed. Rebuilding the UKI can therefore keep pointing to the now-deleted swapfile; later setup may add a second, conflicting resume value. This occurs on the upgrade branch where effective default root= was missing and the booted cmdline carried resume. On the next remove run the hook marker is gone, so there is no cleanup retry. Suggested fix: inspect and remove only the stale Omarchy hibernation tokens from other effective cmdline sources, in particular the line the Quattro upgrade wrote, preserving root/unlock options, then verify the effective cmdline.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus N1 (upgrade/3.x /etc/default/limine resume params). Kept as source-only optional note.

leads.summary: Missing or malformed mkinitcpio hook prevents cleaning an extant resume drop-in
leads.consequence: If the hook was removed separately, failed to install, or no longer contains the exact line, but resume.conf still exists, remove prints 'Hibernation is not set up', returns 0, and never reaches lines 54-60. The stale resume kernel parameters remain active on rebuilds and a future setup still refuses to rewrite the old offset because it sees the existing file. Suggested fix: let the presence of either drop-in trigger cleanup and guard hook deletion independently; test a leftover-drop-in-only state.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus F1, reproduced by Opus; main finding.

leads.summary: Deleting the entire resume.conf can remove user-supplied boot-critical settings
leads.consequence: Setup leaves any pre-existing resume.conf untouched and still marks setup as configured, without checking ownership or contents. The new remove deletes that file wholesale whenever it is a regular file. If it also contains a custom root= or unlock parameter, that option disappears from the rebuilt UKI and the next boot can fail, and any other custom parameters are lost. This is conditional on that file being user-maintained; the stock setup-created file contains only the resume line. Suggested fix: only delete a drop-in that exactly matches the generated format, otherwise remove just Omarchy's resume tokens with a warning or leave custom content for manual reconciliation.
leads.triage: dropped; resume.conf is written only by Omarchy setup and also deleted by factory reset (Opus Q2, rg). A user-authored file at that path is hypothetical.

leads.summary: Failed deletion or a skipped UKI rebuild is reported as successful removal
leads.consequence: The script has no errexit or explicit check. If deleting resume.conf fails, it still rebuilds from the stale drop-in; if rebuilding fails, it still prints 'Hibernation removed' and exits successfully. More subtly, limine-mkinitcpio 1.40.0 converts a per-kernel failed build to success by skipping it, so checking its process exit alone cannot establish that every old UKI was replaced. The marker has already been deleted, making the next remove invocation exit early without retrying. The user may boot an old UKI with resume= for a deleted swapfile. Suggested fix: propagate deletion and build failures, and verify rebuilt target kernel entries or embedded cmdlines before reporting success, with a retry path that does not depend on the deleted marker.
leads.triage: dropped; Unchecked rm/rebuild status is the pre-existing pattern of the script (no set -e, prior rm unchecked); not introduced by this PR and low value.

leads.summary: The setup-created rtc-alarm.conf remains after hibernation removal
leads.consequence: On s2idle machines setup writes rtc_cmos.use_acpi_alarm=1 in rtc-alarm.conf for suspend-then-hibernate. Remove deletes only resume.conf, leaving that option in the newly built command line and in the next setup's absent-only path. This is an incomplete undo of setup, although a user might separately want the flag for ordinary suspend, so removal should be explicit about ownership and preserve a customised file. Suggested fix: decide whether the setup-owned RTC drop-in belongs to removal, and delete it before the rebuild if it does, with an ownership check if local edits must be preserved.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus N2; design choice, omitted from comment.

leads.summary: New source-grep test passes when actual resume.conf deletion is disabled
leads.consequence: The test checks only path mentions and the location of the text 'sudo rm "$RESUME_DROP_IN"'; it never invokes remove or inspects the file at rebuild time. A plausible disabled-deletion mutant (`: # sudo rm "$RESUME_DROP_IN"`) still prints both pass lines, despite preserving the stale parameter. Suggested fix: use a sandboxed fixture with synthetic /etc and swap paths and stubbed sudo/limine-mkinitcpio to assert file absence at the rebuild; include missing-hook and failed-removal cases.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_coordinator; Test greps the literal string 'sudo rm "$RESUME_DROP_IN"' with grep -n, which also matches a commented-out line (head/test/shell.d/hibernation-remove-test.sh:15). Sol mutant run plan2/runs/20260928T225447Z-1ad4ad39. Published as Optional test improvement, with Opus's textual-test limit (N3).

leads.summary: Unstacked open hibernation PRs conflict at this exact removal hunk
leads.consequence: These changes are not stacked. #8199 and #12155 independently delete resume.conf plus rtc-alarm.conf, and #10065 also adds GPU-defer-hook removal. A three-way merge against each PR's own base produces conflict markers in the modified removal code. #13610 also conflicts at the same removal hunk, but adds UPower critical-hibernate cleanup that must not be discarded during resolution. Merging either side blindly can reintroduce duplicate removal, lose RTC/GPU cleanup, or leave the UPower override active after hibernation is removed. GitHub marks #8199, #12155 and #13610 MERGEABLE against their own base, not against this PR, while #10065 is already CONFLICTING. Suggested fix: coordinate these overlapping fixes and merge both sides' distinct cleanup operations with a combined fixture; do not treat #8199 as an independent duplicate fix after merging this PR.
leads.triage: partly_corroborated_extended; #8199/#12155 in Opus F2. #10065 and #13610 conflicts verified by coordinator git merge-file (2 and 1 conflicts) in triage-merge.wf4P/. Added as optional note.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Machines that already ran the old remove keep the stale `resume_offset`.

### Existing leftover `resume.conf` is not repaired

The old remove deleted `omarchy_resume.conf` but left `resume.conf`. There, the fixed remove exits with "Hibernation is not set up", and setup still skips `resume.conf` when it exists (line 131), so re-setup keeps the old offset. **Impact:** #13583 persists for machines already in that state (see #10037, #10374, #12096).

**Suggested change:** drop setup's `if [[ ! -f $RESUME_DROP_IN ]]` guard so a fresh setup rewrites `resume.conf` from the current swapfile.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at e870b4b)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/hibernation-stale-resume-test.sh` at the PR head (e870b4b3) and run `bash test/shell.d/hibernation-stale-resume-test.sh`. It runs the real `omarchy-hibernation-remove` and `omarchy-hibernation-setup`, with their hard-coded system paths rewritten into a temp directory and `sudo`, `btrfs`, `swapon`, `swapoff`, `swaplabel`, `findmnt`, `chattr`, `gum` and `limine-mkinitcpio` stubbed. It starts from the state the pre-fix remove leaves behind (no resume hook, `resume.conf` with the old offset), then runs the fixed remove and a new setup whose swapfile maps to a different offset.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

# A machine that ran the old remove has resume.conf but no resume hook. After
# updating, running remove and then setup again must not keep the deleted
# swapfile's resume_offset.

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
fake="$tmp/root"
stub="$tmp/bin"
mkdir -p "$stub" "$fake/etc/limine-entry-tool.d" "$fake/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d" \
  "$fake/sys/power" "$fake/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep"

cat >"$stub/sudo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
# Unprivileged test: drop the root ownership flags install_root_file passes.
if [[ $1 == "/usr/bin/install" ]]; then
  shift
  args=()
  while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
      -o | -g) shift 2 ;;
      *) args+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
  done
  exec /usr/bin/install "${args[@]}"
fi
exec "$@"
SH
cat >"$stub/btrfs" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
case "$1 $2" in
  "subvolume show") [[ -f $3/.subvolume ]] ;;
  "subvolume create") mkdir -p "$3" && touch "$3/.subvolume" ;;
  "subvolume delete") rm -rf -- "$3" ;;
  "filesystem mkswapfile") : >"${@: -1}" ;;
  "inspect-internal map-swapfile") [[ -f ${@: -1} ]] && echo "$NEW_OFFSET" ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
SH
printf '#!/bin/bash\n[[ -f $1 ]]\n' >"$stub/swaplabel"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho /dev/mapper/root\n' >"$stub/findmnt"
for cmd in gum swapon swapoff chattr limine-mkinitcpio; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stub/$cmd"
done
chmod +x "$stub"/*

# The helpers hard-code system paths; run copies pointed at the scratch root.
for helper in omarchy-hibernation-remove omarchy-hibernation-setup; do
  sed -e "s#/etc/#$fake/etc/#g" \
    -e "s#/sys/power/#$fake/sys/power/#g" \
    -e "s#/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/#$fake/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/#g" \
    -e "s#\"/swap\"#\"$fake/swap\"#" \
    -e "s#\"/swap/swapfile\"#\"$fake/swap/swapfile\"#" \
    "$ROOT/bin/$helper" >"$tmp/$helper"
  if sed "s#$fake#@#g" "$tmp/$helper" | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' |
    grep -qE '(^|[^@[:alnum:]_])/(etc|sys|swap|usr/lib/systemd)([/"]|$)'; then
    fail "$helper only touches the scratch root"
  fi
done

# State left by the old remove: swapfile, subvolume, fstab entry and resume
# hook are gone, resume.conf still has the old swapfile's offset.
printf 'UUID=root / btrfs rw 0 0\n' >"$fake/etc/fstab"
printf '1000\n' >"$fake/sys/power/image_size"
printf 's2idle [deep]\n' >"$fake/sys/power/mem_sleep"
echo 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=1929151"' \
  >"$fake/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf"

run() {
  PATH="$stub:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" NEW_OFFSET=2222222 bash "$tmp/$1" "${@:2}" 2>&1
}

remove_output=$(run omarchy-hibernation-remove)
run omarchy-hibernation-setup --force >/dev/null

grep -Fq 'resume_offset=2222222"' "$fake/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf" ||
  fail "setup after an earlier remove points resume_offset at the new swapfile" \
    "remove printed: $remove_output"$'\n'"resume.conf after setup: $(<"$fake/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf")"
pass "setup after an earlier remove points resume_offset at the new swapfile"
```

Actual output at e870b4b3 (exit 1):

```
remove printed: Hibernation is not set up
resume.conf after setup: KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=1929151"
not ok - setup after an earlier remove points resume_offset at the new swapfile
```

The same test fails the same way at the base (b18ab495). With the `if [[ ! -f $RESUME_DROP_IN ]]; then` guard at `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup` line 131 replaced by `if true; then`, it prints:

```
ok - setup after an earlier remove points resume_offset at the new swapfile
```

and the PR's own `hibernation-remove-test.sh` still passes on that tree:

```
ok - hibernation remove deletes the resume drop-ins setup writes
ok - hibernation remove drops resume parameters before rebuilding the UKI
```
</details>

### Overlaps open #8199 and #12155

#8199 makes the same removal and adds a test at the same path; #12155 adds an equivalent block. Both conflict with this PR's remove. **Impact:** only one can land as is.

**Suggested change:** coordinate with #8199 and list the older issues the chosen fix closes.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- On a machine that has not yet run remove, `resume.conf` is now deleted before `sudo limine-mkinitcpio`, and a stubbed setup/remove/setup cycle writes the new offset (the base keeps the old one).
- limine-entry-tool 1.40.0 builds the UKI and limine.conf cmdline from its config layers, so deleting the drop-in drops the params unless another layer carries them.
- The new test is auto-registered, fails at the base and passes at the head.
- `./test/cli` stops at `vscode generated theme references current theme file` at both base and head, as described.

**Optional notes:**
- **Optional test improvement:** the new test is textual. It still passes with the deletion commented out (`# sudo rm "$RESUME_DROP_IN"`) and does not catch the leftover-state case above; a stubbed setup/remove/setup run in the reproducer's style covers both.
- Machines upgraded from 3.x may also carry `resume=`/`resume_offset=` in `/etc/default/limine`, which limine-entry-tool reads after the drop-ins and which this PR leaves in place. Source reading only, not run.
- #10065 and #13610 also edit `bin/omarchy-hibernation-remove` and conflict textually with this PR.
</details>
